label: Crude birth rate
reliability_criteria: Canonical tier = UN DYB Table 9 crude birth rates across 13 editions (2011-2015 + 2017-2024, 2016 FILEPASS-encrypted and unwired), 2007-2024, computed by the UN Statistics Division from the countries' own registered births and republished as reported (rates only for completeness codes C/|, the collector's own editorial rule); witness tier = UN WPP estimates via the World Bank's SP.DYN.CBRT.IN (modeled, ~200 countries, 1960-2024). Authenticity first per ADR-0008: displayed beside each other, never blended.
license: Mixed, per source (see "sources"): UN DYB = UN data reuse policy (attribution required, no endorsement implied); World Bank witness = CC-BY-4.0.
notes:
THE NINTH INDICATOR, THE CBR COMPANION (v15). The corpus's #1 metric (birth_rate_fertility, 111 citations, 16/16 books) is TFR — v14 settled that. But the corpus's own 19th-century rows read the CRUDE birth rate ("Crude birth rate milestones: France < 30/1 000, Europe 30-38/1 000 (19th c.)", "Crude birth rate by community in colonial Algeria"), the measure the era's statistical offices actually printed — and the two are NOT convertible: CBR (births per 1,000 total population) drags the age structure along (a young country prints high CBR at moderate fertility, an old country prints low CBR at the same TFR), which is precisely why they ride as TWO indicators, never as a unit conversion. This one is todd_core=false on purpose: no corpus metric carries the crude rate as its own id — the 19th-century CBR rows live under birth_rate_fertility's umbrella, and the companion_indicators link carries the relationship (the board reads them side by side).
CANONICAL TIER: the collector's own natalité print, DYB Table 9 — the same wide layout as Table 15 (Total/Urban/Rural rows, quality-code column, 5-year windows per edition, footnotes worksheet), 13 editions 2007-2024 with the standard vintage arbitration. The collector's honest degradations ride as-reported: "U"-coded countries print birth counts with "..." rates (explicit gap points), the '*' provisional flag and glued '*NN' star-plus-ref markers travel on the points (the v15 grammar find: a provisional birth count citing its own note in one cell, 26 live occurrences across editions 2011/2017-2022), and the countries that stop answering freeze (the questionnaire's own gaps — the US absent from recent Table 9s, the same hole as Table 15). THE COLLECTOR'S CROSS-TABLE DEPENDENCY: these same Table 9 births are the denominator of Table 17's maternal mortality ratios — the UNSD computes both from one questionnaire, which is why this table, not a modeled series, is the canonical CBR.
WITNESS TIER: one door, the minimal honest choice — WDI's WPP redistribution (bare code, 1960-2024, worldwide), the face the collector's honest partiality cannot serve (Todd's Muslim-world and Central-Asia comparisons live here, on the modeled layer). The WPP CBR is structure-carrying and vintage-unpinned (silent revisions, the same limit as the TFR witness); where the tiers agree it is because WPP anchors on the national registration series.
HONEST SCOPE LIMITS: no 19th-century history on the canonical tier (the wired editions start 2007 — Todd's 30/1 000 France milestone of the 1870s-1910s is BOOK data, territory for the curated tier); no 1991-2006 window (the PDF-era editions, the same deliberate boundary as Table 15); Russia's freeze reads on this table too where the questionnaire stopped.
